To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the bound states of a pair of FGSs are linearly stable or weakly oscillatory unstable if they are separated by even and odd numbers of empty potential wells, respectively, and (ii) the bound states with exponentially unstable linear spectra are transformed into long-lived pulsating states.
the gap soliton complexes of the first class are unstable for odd number of separating potential periods and the second class are unstable for even number of separating potential wells.
the gap soliton complexes of the first and the second classes are exponentially (linearly) unstable if the number of separating empty potential wells is odd (even).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability properties of the stationary localized solutions in the NLSE with periodic potential.
the stability of stationary gap soliton complexes (bound states of fundamental gap solitonic modes) in the NLSE with periodic potential and nonlinearity.
stability of gap soliton bound states in the NLSE with periodic potential and nonlinearity of repulsive type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the gap solitonic structures considered in the paper are stable against small perturbations.

the gap soliton complexes of the first and the second classes are linearly exponentially unstable if the number of the separating empty potential wells is odd or even, respectively, and linearly weakly oscillatory unstable if the number is even or odd, respectively.
the FGSs of the first class are stable if they are separated by an even number of empty potential well whereas the second class of modes is stable if the number of separating wells is odd.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stability properties of the bound states of FGSs depend crucially on the number of empty wells separating them.
the linear stability analysis is a powerful tool for prediction of nonlinear behavior of localized modes for the periodic NLSE with the repulsive nonlineary.
the linear stability analysis is in good agreement with the results of numerical simulations for both exponentially and weakly unstable gap solitons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stability properties of the gap soliton complexes are sensitive to the number of the empty wells separating the FGSs, as well as to the distance between FSGs.
the gap soliton complexes are more likely to be stable in repulsive nonlinear media than in attractive media.
, in the case of repulsive nonlinearty, the stability of gap soliton pairs is determined by the parity of the number of separating periods of a periodic potential.
